tutorial.title: Dogs as Pets
tutorial.text: Dogs have been loyal companions to humans for thousands of years. They can be trained to follow commands, do tricks, and even help people with disabilities. Dogs need daily exercise, fresh water, and nutritious food to stay healthy. Many families choose dogs as pets because they are friendly, playful, and protective of the people they love.

passages.title: Ocean Coral Reefs
passages.text: Coral reefs are underwater ecosystems built by tiny animals called coral polyps. These polyps produce a hard limestone skeleton that forms the structure of the reef over hundreds of years. Coral reefs are home to about 25 percent of all ocean species, even though they cover less than one percent of the ocean floor. Fish, sea turtles, sharks, and thousands of other creatures depend on coral reefs for food and shelter. Unfortunately, rising ocean temperatures and pollution are causing many reefs to bleach and die, threatening the survival of countless marine species.

passages.title: The Secret Life of Honey Bees
passages.text: A honey bee colony works like a well-organized city, with every bee playing a specific role to keep the hive alive. The queen lays up to 2,000 eggs per day, while worker bees gather nectar, build honeycomb, and guard the entrance. Scout bees perform a special waggle dance to tell other bees exactly where to find the best flowers. Bees must visit about two million flowers just to make one pound of honey. Without honey bees pollinating crops, humans would lose about one-third of the foods we eat every day.

passages.title: How Earthquakes Happen
passages.text: The surface of the Earth is made up of giant slabs of rock called tectonic plates that are constantly moving, though usually too slowly for us to feel. When two plates push against each other, pull apart, or slide sideways, pressure builds up along the edges. Eventually the pressure becomes too great and the rocks suddenly snap or shift, releasing energy in the form of seismic waves. These waves travel through the ground and cause the shaking we feel during an earthquake. Scientists use instruments called seismographs to measure how strong an earthquake is and to help predict where future quakes might occur.

passages.title: The Printing Press Changed Everything
passages.text: Before Johannes Gutenberg invented the printing press around 1440, every book in Europe had to be copied by hand, which took months and made books extremely expensive. Gutenberg's machine used small metal letters that could be arranged into words, inked, and pressed onto paper to create identical copies quickly. Within fifty years, millions of books were printed across Europe, and suddenly ordinary people could afford to read. The printing press helped spread new ideas about science, religion, and government faster than ever before. Many historians believe it was one of the most important inventions in human history because it changed how knowledge was shared forever.
